subject.title: [Feature]: bearer token authentication for proxy servers

question: Should OpenClaw add native mobile reverse-proxy transport authentication, and which initial modes plus credential lifecycle rules are approved?
rationale: The implementation crosses a security boundary before Gateway pairing/auth, and automation cannot choose storage, reset, redaction, secure-transport, static-header/cookie, or OIDC redirect policy safely.

options.title: Approve a static-header first slice
options.body: Start with bearer/basic or explicit static headers for Android/iOS manual and setup-code flows, with secure storage, reset/endpoint-change clearing, redaction, secure-transport guards, and live reverse-proxy proof.

options.title: Limit scope to iOS Basic auth
options.body: Let the narrower iOS Basic-auth PR proceed as a partial fix while keeping this broad issue open for Android, bearer/static headers, cookies, and OIDC.

options.title: Pause for OIDC-centered design
options.body: Hold implementation until maintainers define a browser/app-link OIDC flow and decide whether static proxy credentials should be supported at all.

recommendation.title: Approve a static-header first slice
recommendation.body: Start with bearer/basic or explicit static headers for Android/iOS manual and setup-code flows, with secure storage, reset/endpoint-change clearing, redaction, secure-transport guards, and live reverse-proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties steipete to setup-code bootstrap, trusted-proxy policy, and the auth contract this feature would extend.
